title: observability-weekly-2026-03-09
content:
Observability team weekly notes — week of 2026-03-09

Attendees: Laura Chen (owner), Marcus Lee, Sofia Martinez, Devon O'Neil, Priya Kapoor, (plus async updates from Ashwin and Rhea)

Summary / high level
- Focus this week: finalize tracing sampling rollout, finish dashboard refresh for model-serving cost telemetry, and stabilize the new Prometheus remote-write pipeline.
- Status: most work in progress but moving toward canary rollout next Tue (2026-03-16) for sampling changes.
- Risks: cost telemetry joins BigQuery export currently experiences ~6 hour lag during peak; need mitigation to avoid stale billing alerts.

Standup highlights (daily snippets)
- Mon 2026-03-09: Marcus: completed Tempo retention config changes; started integration tests for span deduping. Sofia: dashboard layout prototype ready; needs dataset joins for token_cost metric. Devon: investigated prometheus scrape spike (cause: kubelet misconfig). Priya: cost-telemetry pipeline PR opened for review.
- Tue 2026-03-10: Marcus: discovered edge-case where service mesh sidecar double-tags traces — PR RDW-obs-214 in review. Sofia: dashboard now shows per-model p95 latency and cost per 1M tokens (approx).
- Wed 2026-03-11: Devon: fixed kubelet exporter misconfig and reduced scrape volume by 35%; alerts cleared. Laura: ran end-to-end test for sampling rules against replay data (100k requests).
- Thu 2026-03-12: Priya: pushed PR to add ingestion timestamp to cost export so BigQuery join can filter by ingestion_time — should reduce appearance of stale rows in dashboard.
- Fri 2026-03-13: Team retrospective on tracing test failures; next week we'll run a longer replay with cross-region traces.

Tracing workstream (Marcus + Laura)
- Goal: shift default sampling from 1.0 to adaptive rate-based sampling for production services to reduce storage and UI load without losing important traces.
- What we did this week:
  - Implemented adaptiveSampler v2 in Tempo config (branch: obs/sampling-v2).
  - Added a safety rule: keep 100% sampling for spans with error tags and sampling overrides for large-latency (p99 > 2s) requests.
  - Ran replay test (~100k synthetic requests) against canary config. Key results: expected trace volume drop ~55%, error traces preserved at ~99.8%.
- Outstanding items:
  - Need to handle double-tagging caused by sidecar (DEV-obs-214). Marcus to get PR merged and coordinate canary restart.
  - Add SLI: ratio of error-span retention after sampling (target >= 99.5%). Owner: Laura. Due: 2026-03-18.

Dashboards (Sofia + Priya)
- Dashboard refresh progress:
  - New model-serving overview dashboard v2 implemented in Grafana. Panels: p50/p95 latency, token throughput, cost-per-1k-tokens, per-model error-rate, trace-link column.
  - Introduced breakdown by deployment tier (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
  - UX tweaks: collapsed rows for low-traffic models to reduce rendering time.
- Known issues:
  - Cost-per-1k-tokens computed from cost telemetry BigQuery export shows occasional duplicate rows -> inflates cost metric. Temporary filter applied (ingestion_time dedupe) in dashboard query.
  - Rendering lag for >80 panels on a single dashboard for SRE on-call devices. Action: split into two dashboards (overview + deep-dive). Owner: Sofia. Due: 2026-03-17.

Cost telemetry (Priya + Devon)
- Goals: reduce cost pipeline lag to <1 hour end-to-end; ensure per-model cost accuracy within 2% for monthly reports.
- What we did:
  - Prometheus -> remote-write -> BigQuery exporter tests completed; found serialization overhead adding ~8–12 minutes per batch under load.
  - Added ingestion_time column (PR merged) to help dedupe and allow dashboards to ignore late-arriving rows older than 2 hours.
  - Implemented a lightweight pre-aggregation in the ingestion service to reduce downstream join cardinality.
- Next steps:
  - Run load test with 10x token throughput to validate pre-aggregation. Owner: Devon. Due: 2026-03-20.
  - Add alert threshold for BigQuery export lag at 60 minutes (currently 240). Owner: Priya. Due: 2026-03-15.

Alerts / incidents
- This week: one P1 (brief) related to Prometheus scrape spike causing delayed rule evaluations (~45m). Root cause: kubelet exporter misconfig on three nodes; fixed by Devon with a rolling restart.
- Action items from incident:
  - Add runbook steps for kubelet exporter misconfig. Owner: DevOps (ticket JIRA-RDW-789).
  - Add synthetic heartbeat metric and alert if Prometheus scrape volume changes >25% within 15m. Owner: SRE. Due: 2026-03-16.

Meetings / decisions
- 2026-03-11 — Tracing sync: agreed to canary adaptive sampler on a subset of services (frontend + auth + inference-router) starting 2026-03-16. Rollout plan: 24h canary -> assess error-span retention -> if stable, scale to all serving lanes over 1 week.
- 2026-03-12 — Dashboard review with product: product asked to include "tokens-per-request" on model overview; Sofia to add a compact panel.
- Decision: keep high-fidelity tracing (100% sampling) for private deployments for first month post-upgrade by default. Owner: Laura.

Blocking items / help needed
- Need a small capacity bump on the Tempo cluster to run replay tests in parallel with production (ops approval required). Ticket: JIRA-RDW-456. Asking infra for +2 CPU, +50Gi storage for 72h.
- Query performance for the cost-per-1k-tokens panel still slow for large time windows (>30d). Might need materialized view in BigQuery. If finance agrees, we'll provision. Contact: Priya to coordinate with finance.

Action items (owner — due)
- Merge sidecar double-tagging fix and roll canary (Marcus — 2026-03-12).
- Add error-span retention SLI and dashboard (Laura — 2026-03-18).
- Split heavy dashboard into overview + deep-dive (Sofia — 2026-03-17).
- Alert for BigQuery export lag at 60m (Priya — 2026-03-15).
- Load test pre-aggregation at 10x throughput (Devon — 2026-03-20).
- Infra approval for Tempo replay capacity (Laura -> infra ticket JIRA-RDW-456 — 2026-03-13).

Notes / links
- Tracing sampling plan (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Tracing+Sampling+Plan
- PR with sidecar fix: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/214
- Incident runbook stub: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Incident+Runbooks
- Dashboard prototype: grafana://dashboards/model-serving-overview-v2

Retro / not-forget
- Replay tests are valuable — schedule longer replays across regions before any global sampling change.
- Keep product in the loop on cost telemetry approximations; surface expected error bounds on dashboards.

Next week priorities
- Start canary sampling rollout 2026-03-16 and monitor retention SLI.
- Finish dashboard split and add tokens-per-request panel.
- Run load test for cost pre-aggregation and follow up on BigQuery materialized view decision.

If you have updates, add them to this doc (comments or bullets) or drop a note in #observability on Slack.

-- Laura
